name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +19 partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Quigley running with large cash advantage
Republican challenger has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago seat with a +19 partisan lean, a $1.2 million war chest, and no meaningful opposition spending, while Hanson has reported no fundraising. Markets price the Democratic win near 98%, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a margin well above 20 points.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly strong national Republican wave could tighten the race, though nothing in the evidence suggests either is likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Chicago-area district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He has raised over $725,000 and holds nearly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Tommy Hanson has reported no fundraising and draws no outside support. No independent groups are spending against Quigley, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Quigley roughly a 98% chance of winning, and the fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s. With no public polling and no signs of a contest, this race sits firmly in the Safe Democratic category.
